core.sign-in-providers.title: Sign-in providers
core.sign-in-providers.description: Let people sign in with an account they already have elsewhere. Set a provider up, check it, then put it in use.
core.sign-in-providers.any-microsoft-and: Any work, school or personal account
core.sign-in-providers.about.google: People sign in with their Google account. You need an OAuth client from a Google Cloud project.
core.sign-in-providers.about.microsoft: People sign in with their Microsoft work, school or personal account. You need an app registration in Microsoft Entra.
core.sign-in-providers.about.oidc: People sign in with another OpenID Connect provider, such as a university's own. You need a client registered with that provider.
core.sign-in-providers.register.title: 1. Register this site with {provider}
core.sign-in-providers.register.google: In Google Cloud, open APIs & Services, then Credentials, and create an OAuth client ID of the type Web application. Add this address under Authorised redirect URIs.
core.sign-in-providers.register.microsof: In the Microsoft Entra admin centre, open App registrations and register a new application. Choose who can use it, then add this address as a Web redirect URI. Under Token configuration, add the optional claims email and xms_edov to the ID token.
core.sign-in-providers.register.oidc: Ask the provider for a client of the confidential (web) type, using the authorisation code flow, and give it this address as its redirect URI.
core.sign-in-providers.client.title: 2. Save its client ID and secret
core.sign-in-providers.client-id-help.mi: The application (client) ID on the app registration's overview.
core.sign-in-providers.client-id-help.oi: The client ID the provider gave this site.
core.sign-in-providers.label: Name on the button
core.sign-in-providers.label-help: People see “Sign in with” and this name, such as your university's.
core.sign-in-providers.discovery-help: The provider's OpenID Connect discovery address, which usually ends /.well-known/openid-configuration. It is checked when you save.
core.sign-in-providers.found.title: Found the issuer {issuer}
core.sign-in-providers.discovery-problem: The issuer and its addresses must use HTTPS.
This provider does not offer the openid and email scopes.
This is not an OpenID Connect discovery document.
The issuer named in the document is not the address it came from.
Nothing answered at the discovery address just now.
core.sign-in-providers.secret-help: From the same OAuth client. It is kept encrypted and never shown again, only its last four characters.
core.sign-in-providers.secret-keep: Leave blank to keep the saved secret
core.sign-in-providers.domains-help.goog: Only Google Workspace accounts from these domains may sign in, such as example.org. Leave empty to accept any Google account.
core.sign-in-providers.domains-help.micr: A Microsoft sign-in joins an existing account by its address only for these domains, such as your university's, and only when Microsoft says the domain's owner verified the address. Anyone else is emailed a code once to prove it.
core.sign-in-providers.domains-help.oidc: A sign-in joins an existing account by its address only for these domains, and only when the provider says the address is verified. Anyone else is emailed a code once to prove it.
core.sign-in-providers.tenants-help: The tenant IDs of the organisations whose accounts may sign in, from each organisation's Entra overview. Leave empty to accept any work or school account.
core.sign-in-providers.personal-help: Such as Outlook.com and Hotmail addresses. They always prove their address by emailed code first.
core.sign-in-providers.managed-domains-h: Addresses in these domains sign in only with {provider} and are never sent a sign-in link. Each must also be a domain it can vouch for, and no other provider's.
core.sign-in-providers.domains-consequen: Anyone whose account belongs to an organisation no longer listed will not be able to sign in with {provider}.
core.sign-in-providers.check.title: 3. Check it
core.sign-in-providers.check.help: Asks {provider} whether it accepts this client ID and secret. It cannot check the redirect URI, so try signing in once it is in use.
core.sign-in-providers.check.passed: {provider} accepted the client ID and secret.
core.sign-in-providers.missing.client-id: Save the client ID before putting it in use.
core.sign-in-providers.missing.secret: Save the client secret before putting it in use.
core.sign-in-providers.missing.both: Save the client ID and secret before putting it in use.
core.sign-in-providers.missing.several: Save its set-up before putting it in use.
core.sign-in-providers.missing.label: Save the name on its button before putting it in use.
core.sign-in-providers.missing.discovery: Save its discovery address before putting it in use.
core.sign-in-tabs.label: Sign-in pages
